import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Downloading Iris dataset...")
    url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaskom/seaborn-data/master/iris.csv"
    df = pd.read_csv(url)
    # Ensure the directory exists before saving
    import os
    if not os.path.exists('data'):
        os.makedirs('data')
    df.to_csv('data/iris.csv', index=False)


# Set a professional and clear style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a pairplot to visualize pairwise relationships and distributions
# This is highly effective for the Iris dataset to see how features separate the species
g = sns.pairplot(
    df,
    hue='species',
    diag_kind='kde',  # Use Kernel Density Estimate for diagonal plots
    markers=["o", "s", "D"],  # Use distinct markers for each species
    plot_kws={'alpha': 0.85, 's': 50, 'edgecolor': 'k'}, # Style scatter plots
    height=2.5
)

# Add a clear, overarching title to the figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    'Pairwise Feature Relationships in the Iris Dataset',
    y=1.03,  # Adjust title position to avoid overlap
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight='bold'
)

# Improve the legend
g._legend.set_title("Species")
for t in g._legend.texts:
    t.set_text(t.get_text().capitalize()) # Capitalize species names

# Save the final figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Close the plot to prevent it from displaying in some environments
plt.close()
